The appeal path, quoted from POL-GEN-04

Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 0.00 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

The judge's explanation, as written

To both parties: this is a route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-00112 (Tampines to Raffles Place). The deviation is established on the trace, but the fare arithmetic leaves nothing to refund, so the charge you paid, Ms Rider, stands. 1. Distance (POL-RD-01). The governing measure is the GPS trace, not the meter's rounded copy. EV-GPS-00112 records 22.40 km against the booked optimal of 17.60 km on EV-TRIP-00112: excess 4.80 km, or 27.27% of optimal. Both limbs are cleared (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. I have not used the trip record's 20.00 km / 13.6%, because POL-RD-01 forbids citing that field for the threshold test; the driver's argument that the excess be measured only from started_at (13.8%) is rejected for the same reason. 2. Fare (POL-RD-02). The fare model is METERED. Recomputed fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.60 + 0.28 x 28.0) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/tolls = 25.64. Charged total = 25.26. Refund = 25.26 - 25.64 = -0.38, floored at zero = 0.00. The optimal route is 4.8 km shorter but 7.8 minutes slower (28.0 optimal vs 20.2 actual), and the higher optimal time charge (7.84 vs the 5.66 billed) more than offsets the extra distance charge; you were not overcharged. A refund below SGD 0.50 is NO_ACTION as de minimis, and under POL-GEN-03 the charge stands as it is. 3. The Paya Lebar Quarter stop. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00112, weight 1.0) shows the request and the driver's 'ok can', but the trace never comes within 200 m of the resolved waypoint - the nearest fix is 512 m away (fix 158, 18:45:00). Under POL-RD-04 the corroboration test fails and POL-RD-14 directs that no distance is excluded; the instruction did not cause the measured excess. The missed stop is a service matter on which this policy pays nothing - no fare line charges a stop or a missed stop. The driver is also wrong to say he made the stop: his own device trace does not support it. 4. Impairment. EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are each impaired at weight 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT (they disagree about when the trip began by 13.5 minutes). That is schema-level impairment only: under POL-RD-07 the trace is policy-clean - no gap over 90 s (longest 0 s), no straight-line jump over 500 m, a 10 s sampling interval - so it still measures the excess, and the impairment enters POL-GEN-02 as a confidence discount, not as an escalation. 5. No escalation. POL-RD-10(1): the fact that decides this ruling - that the fare recomputation yields no refund - is carried by EV-FARE-00112 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0, line items reconciling to the cent); the 0.4 impairment goes to the measured actual distance, and the outcome is NO_ACTION whether or not a deviation is established. POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged, the trace being policy-clean. POL-RD-10(4) is not engaged: the pickup and dropoff events on the two records align (18:17:50 / 18:18:40 and 18:52:20 / 18:52:12); the divergence is the meter start, not a pickup or dropoff timestamp. POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged: the driver's 'the app was acting up' excuse cites no advisory, and POL-RD-13 makes an uncited traffic assertion weightless rather than an escalation. POL-RD-10(7) is confined by POL-RD-14: a request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent, not contradictory evidence. The rider's arguments for escalation on the 0.4 cap and on the started_at conflict are therefore rejected. 6. Other claims. No repeat-deviation pattern arises (1 flag over 296 trips in 90 days; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field POL-RD-06 names), so there is no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral. There are no ERP gantries, tolls, airport surcharge or promo lines, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct. The driver's compensation claim (2.4 unbilled km x 0.75 = 1.80) is declined: it rests entirely on the 0.4-weighted trace and on exactly the disputed pre-start segment, so it cannot be granted above the confidence floor. The monetary effect is nil, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00. Either party may appeal this provisional ruling under POL-GEN-04. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).

What each side argued

The rider advocate

kept The driver's own trace measures 22.40 km against the booked optimal of 17.60 km — an excess of 4.80 km, or 27.27% of optimal. That clears both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate (more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence and the driver must answer for it. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is IMPAIRED on the admissibility pre-pass, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4; the impairment is one of alignment with the trip record, not of trace quality, and the excess figure stands as the trace's own measurement.

evidence EV-GPS-00112 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The trip record's 20.0 km and 13.6% may not be used against the threshold. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field and says in terms that trip_record.actual_distance_km 'may NOT be cited for the threshold test' because it is a rounded convenience copy. The fare ledger confirms these are two different measurements, noting that distance_charged_km of 20.00 is not a copy of the 22.40 km trace. Where the two figures straddle the 20% gate — as the admissibility report itself observes — the trace figure governs and the excess is 27.27%, not 13.6%. I disclose that both EV-TRIP-00112 and EV-GPS-00112 carry CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT at weight_multiplier 0.4.

evidence EV-TRIP-00112, EV-GPS-00112 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The trace is schema-impaired but clean for policy purposes, and so may measure the excess. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) look for a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m between consecutive fixes, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. EV-GPS-00112 reports an empty gaps array, max_gap_sec of 0.0, 100.0% coverage and a 10.0 second sample interval, so none of those limbs fires: the POL-RD-07 consequences and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation are not engaged, and the trace remains the instrument that measures the excess. The artifact is nonetheless IMPAIRED (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4), which I disclose; that is a POL-GEN-02 confidence down-weight and nothing more.

evidence EV-GPS-00112 · clauses POL-RD-07, POL-GEN-02

discarded The driver blames the evening — 'the app was acting up' — but no external-traffic explanation is on file for this trip. EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0: no LTA advisory covers the PIE or the ECP in the 18:14–18:52 window on 4 August 2026, which are the corridors the booked optimal route uses. Under POL-RD-13 an asserted traffic cause is tested against the trip's traffic_advisory and nothing else, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Nothing here reduces the measured excess.

evidence EV-ADVIS-00112-01 · clauses POL-RD-13, POL-RD-03, POL-RD-08

Discarded by the referee (IMPAIRMENT_UNDISCLOSED): the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-00112-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

kept My client did ask for the Paya Lebar Quarter stop and the driver agreed in terms ('ok can', MSG-00112-002, sent 18:33:30). But a rider instruction exonerates distance only if the trace corroborates it: POL-RD-04 requires the vehicle to pass within 200 m of chat_message.waypoint_hint, resolved here to VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER. It never did — the nearest fix to that waypoint is 512.35 m away (fix index 158, at 18:45:00) against the 200 m threshold. Under POL-RD-14 an instruction the trace does not corroborate caused nothing: no distance is excluded and the excess stands as measured. EV-GPS-00112 is IMPAIRED (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4) and I disclose it; the waypoint distances are its own derived field.

evidence EV-CHAT-00112, EV-GPS-00112 · clauses POL-RD-04, POL-RD-14

kept The driver says he 'did make the PLQ stop... waited about four minutes there'. His device says otherwise: the closest the vehicle comes to the PLQ waypoint is 512 m and the trace shows no dwell there, so his account of compliance fails on the very artifact that would have proved it. On POL-RD-14 the instruction is found and not corroborated, and under POL-RD-08 a driver assertion that points to no supporting artifact discharges nothing. What the trace does prove is my client's grievance — she asked for the stop and the vehicle never went near it. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is IMPAIRED (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4).

evidence EV-GPS-00112, EV-CHAT-00112 · clauses POL-RD-14, POL-RD-08

kept The two admitted records disagree about when this trip began by more than the 10-minute limb of POL-RD-10(4): EV-TRIP-00112's started_at is 18:32:10, while EV-GPS-00112's first fix is at 18:18:40 — 13 minutes 30 seconds earlier — and 2.38 km of trace falls inside a period the trip record says had not started. The disagreement is outcome-determinative: over the whole trace the excess is 27.27% and the POL-RD-01 gate is cleared; measured from started_at only 20.02 km was driven and the excess is 13.8%, below the gate. POL-RD-10 makes escalation terminal and holds the disputed amount rather than collecting it, which is the only course that does not leave my client paying a charge this record cannot justify. What would resolve it is a record-type item: the device event log for DRV-03187 distinguishing a late meter start from the tail of a previous job, or a corrected trip start. Both cited artifacts are IMPAIRED, issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4, which I disclose.

evidence EV-TRIP-00112, EV-GPS-00112 · clauses POL-RD-10

kept Independently of POL-RD-10(4), no merits ruling can be issued at or above the platform's 0.70 confidence floor. The fact this dispute turns on — the excess — is carried by EV-GPS-00112 (22.40 km driven) and EV-TRIP-00112 (17.60 km optimal), each at weight_multiplier 0.4 on the pre-pass. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence may not exceed the weight_multiplier of the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, which here is 0.4, so POL-RD-10(1) is engaged and the case goes to a human reviewer with the amount held. Both cited artifacts are IMPAIRED with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and I disclose that.

evidence EV-GPS-00112, EV-TRIP-00112 · clauses POL-GEN-02, POL-RD-10

The driver advocate

kept POL-RD-01 measures the excess as the length of the gps_trace polyline between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, and it is the trace, not the rounded meter copy, that governs. On this trip the recorded pickup event is the trip record's started_at of 18:32:10, while the trace runs from 18:18:40 to 18:52:12, so 2.38 km of the trace lies before the trip the platform recorded. On the assessor's own alignment figures for that artifact the segment actually driven is 20.02 km, an excess of 2.42 km, or 13.8% of the 17.6 km booked optimal - under the 20% limb of POL-RD-01. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs to pass; the percentage limb fails, so the excess is not established and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The whole-trace figures of 4.80 km and 27.3% (derived.deviation) are an artefact of counting that 2.38 km head, which is exactly why the pre-pass records that the interpretation moves the measured excess across the POL-RD-01 threshold. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are both IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

evidence EV-GPS-00112, EV-TRIP-00112 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept Even if the tribunal takes the whole trace as the measured trip and holds the deviation established, POL-RD-02 returns nothing to the rider. The fare model is METERED, so the recomputation runs on this trip's own figures: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 + 0.28 x 28.0) x 1.0 surge, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP, tolls, surcharges, waiting fee and promo = 25.64, against a charged_total of 25.26. Refund = charged_total - recomputed_fare = -0.38, floored at zero; a refund below SGD 0.50 is NO_ACTION as de minimis. The fare_breakdown's own derived money block carries the same result (recomputed_fare 25.6400, refund payable 0.00, below_de_minimis true). The booked optimal figures are the booking-time estimate carried on that money block; the CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT flagged on EV-TRIP-00112 (IMPAIRED, 0.4) goes to the measured actual distance, not to the booking-time optimal route or to any charged line. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves the charge standing exactly as it is.

evidence EV-FARE-00112 · clauses POL-RD-02, POL-GEN-03

kept The reason the recomputation exceeds what was charged is visible line by line, and it is the rider's own time, not the driver's distance, that is the source. The optimal route - PIE westbound then ECP - is 17.6 km but 28.0 minutes, while the rider was charged for 20.2 minutes. The optimal-route time charge is 7.84 (28.0 x 0.28) against the 5.66 actually billed (20.2 x 0.28); that single line more than offsets the 1.80 of extra distance charge (20.0 km x 0.75 = 15.00 against 17.6 km x 0.75 = 13.20). Net of the two, the rider paid 0.38 LESS than the fare model says the optimal route would have cost.

evidence EV-FARE-00112 · clauses POL-RD-02

kept There is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction to add on top of a zero distance-and-time refund. The fare_breakdown itemises no ERP gantry, no toll, no airport surcharge (this trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), no waiting-time fee and no promo discount; erp_gantries is empty and both the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP totals are 0.00. No charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or the trip record. POL-RD-09 therefore has nothing to correct on this trip and the billing-integrity limb of POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged.

evidence EV-FARE-00112 · clauses POL-RD-09

kept There is no repeat-deviation pattern, so the POL-RD-06 uplift and conduct referral do not apply. The clause's test runs on driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d: this driver carries 1 flag over 296 completed trips in the trailing 90 days. That is below the 3-flag limb and far below the 0.05 ratio limb, and POL-GEN-01 forbids using any other profile field - or the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags - for this test. The clause's consult trigger is not met on materiality either: even on the whole-trace reading the excess is 27.3% and 4.80 km, whereas a MATERIAL deviation requires more than 50% or more than 8.0 km.

evidence EV-DPROF-00112 · clauses POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01

kept Separately from any exoneration, the compensation limb of POL-RD-04 is engaged on the artifacts' own figures: the fare_breakdown billed the rider for distance_charged_km of 20.0 (weight 1.0) while the gps_trace records trace_distance_km of 22.4, a shortfall of 2.4 unbilled kilometres, above the 1.0 km threshold. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is SGD 1.80, rounded up to the nearest 0.05 and within the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. Disclosure: the 22.4 km figure is carried by EV-GPS-00112, which is IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, so this limb is asserted on a down-weighted trace and is worth what that discount says it is worth.

evidence EV-FARE-00112, EV-GPS-00112 · clauses POL-RD-04, POL-GEN-02

kept On the rider's PLQ request the driver does not press an exoneration he cannot corroborate. The chat log shows the rider's request in MSG-00112-001, carrying a resolved waypoint_hint at Paya Lebar Quarter (VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER), and the driver's 'ok can' in MSG-00112-002 - so POL-RD-04(a) and (c) are met - but the trace's nearest fix to that waypoint is 512.35 m away (fix 158, 18:45:00), well outside the 200 m corroboration radius POL-RD-04 sets. The corroboration limb cannot be run on this record, no distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded, and POL-RD-14 directs that the instruction was made and did not reduce the measured excess. What does not follow is any refund: no fare line charges a stop fee or a missed-stop fee, and in any event the distance-and-time lines recompute to zero, so the missed stop is a service matter on which this policy pays nothing. evidence EV-CHAT-00112, EV-GPS-00112, EV-FARE-00112 · clauses POL-RD-04, POL-RD-14

discarded The uncorroborated detour request is not an escalation trigger. POL-RD-10(7) is confined by POL-RD-14 to the case where the trace corroborates the rider's instruction in part, so that the excess attributable to it cannot be separated from the rest. Here the trace corroborates nothing about the waypoint, and a request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent with each other - that is a failed corroboration under POL-RD-04, not two contradictory bodies of comparable evidence. POL-RD-14 directs that the deviation be decided under POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 on the trace as measured, which also disposes of POL-GEN-07: a clause of the policy in force does license an outcome on these facts, so no residual-principles escalation is open.

evidence EV-CHAT-00112, EV-GPS-00112 · clauses POL-RD-14, POL-RD-10, POL-GEN-07

What diverges is the meter start (18:32:10) and the trace's first fix, i.e. the pre-start segment; that is the schema-level CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT the pre-pass has already priced at weight 0.4 under POL-GEN-02, and it does not meet POL-RD-07(a) to (c) at all - the trace has no gaps, a longest gap of 0 seconds and a 10 second sampling interval against a 30 second limb - so it carries POL-GEN-02 consequences only and does not engage POL-RD-07's or POL-RD-10(3)'s consequences. Each draft's own explanation

To the rider and the driver: this dispute cannot be decided on the present record, so it goes to a human reviewer and the disputed SGD 6.00 is held, not collected or refunded. The ruling is ESCALATE under POL-RD-10, which is terminal — no refund and no compensation issues today. Two independent triggers fire. POL-RD-10(4). The trip record (EV-TRIP-00112) says this trip began at 18:32:10; the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00112) begins moving at 18:18:40 and covers 2.38 km before that recorded start. That is a 13 min 30 s disagreement about when the trip began, beyond POL-RD-10(4)'s 10-minute limb, and it is outcome-determinative: over the whole trace the excess is 22.40 − 17.60 = 4.80 km, or 27.27% of the 17.60 km booked optimal, which clears POL-RD-01's 20% and 0.8 km gates; measured from started_at only 20.02 km was driven, an excess of 2.42 km or 13.8%, which fails the 20% gate. The admissibility report records that nothing in the bundle decides whether the meter started late or the trace carries the tail of a previous job. POL-RD-10(1). Independently, the excess is carried only by EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112, each weighted 0.4 (IMPAIRED, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT), so no merits ruling could be issued at or above the 0.70 floor. On the points I could decide: POL-RD-07 (both sides). EV-GPS-00112 is IMPAIRED on the admissibility pre-pass (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4) but is clean for policy purposes: no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, 100% coverage, 10 s sampling interval. POL-RD-07(a)-(c) does not fire, so neither POL-RD-07's consequences nor POL-RD-10(3) is engaged; the 0.4 is a POL-GEN-02 down-weight only. Both things are true and I say both, as POL-GEN-02(3) requires. POL-RD-01 (both sides). Where the trace and the rounded meter copy straddle the gate, the trace governs — trace_distance_km 22.40, not trip_record.actual_distance_km 20.00 — but which stretch of the trace is this trip is the very question the record cannot answer, so the excess cannot be fixed at either 27.27% or 13.8%. POL-RD-02 (driver). The arithmetic is right and would return nothing: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 17.60 + 0.28 × 28.0) × 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 = 25.64 against charged_total 25.26, floored at zero and below the 0.50 de minimis. Because escalation is terminal this does not become the ruling. POL-RD-04 / POL-RD-14 (both). The rider's Paya Lebar Quarter request is in the chat (MSG-00112-001, waypoint_hint VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER) and the driver agreed ('ok can', MSG-00112-002), but the trace's nearest fix to that waypoint is 512.35 m, outside POL-RD-04's 200 m radius. The instruction is found and not corroborated: POL-RD-04 does not apply, no distance is excluded, and the deviation stands as measured (POL-RD-14). No fare line charges a stop or missed-stop fee, so the missed stop pays nothing. POL-RD-04 compensation limb (driver). The 2.4 km gap between the billed 20.0 km and the trace's 22.40 km is the same disputed 2.38 km head. It rests on the impaired trace and on the very interpretation the record cannot settle; it is not awarded, and escalation is in any event terminal. POL-RD-13 / POL-RD-08 (driver's 'app was acting up'). No traffic advisory covers the trip window: EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0. The assertion has no artifact behind it and carries no weight; it neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal. The driver's statement that he made the PLQ stop and waited four minutes is contradicted by the trace, which never approaches the waypoint; that is a conduct question for the reviewer, not a ground of decision here. POL-RD-09 (driver). No ERP gantry, toll, surcharge, waiting fee or promo is itemised; there is nothing to correct and no billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4). POL-RD-06 (driver). No repeat pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d 296, below both limbs, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. Only the fields POL-GEN-01 names were used. POL-GEN-02 cap (driver). I do not accept that the deciding fact sits only on the clean fare breakdown. The 25.64 recomputation is built on optimal_distance_km 17.60 and optimal_duration_min 28.0, which are carried on the impaired trip record, so the cap is not 1.0. What would resolve it: a record-type item — the device event log for DRV-03187 distinguishing a late meter start from a previous job's tail, or a corrected trip start — would let the reviewer fix the excess and then run the POL-RD-02 arithmetic. No referral is recorded, because no clause produces one on these facts.
To both parties: this is a route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-00112 (Tampines to Raffles Place). The deviation is established on the trace, but the fare arithmetic leaves nothing to refund, so the charge you paid, Ms Rider, stands. 1. Distance (POL-RD-01). The governing measure is the GPS trace, not the meter's rounded copy. EV-GPS-00112 records 22.40 km against the booked optimal of 17.60 km on EV-TRIP-00112: excess 4.80 km, or 27.27% of optimal. Both limbs are cleared (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. I have not used the trip record's 20.00 km / 13.6%, because POL-RD-01 forbids citing that field for the threshold test; the driver's argument that the excess be measured only from started_at (13.8%) is rejected for the same reason. 2. Fare (POL-RD-02). The fare model is METERED. Recomputed fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.60 + 0.28 x 28.0) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/tolls = 25.64. Charged total = 25.26. Refund = 25.26 - 25.64 = -0.38, floored at zero = 0.00. The optimal route is 4.8 km shorter but 7.8 minutes slower (28.0 optimal vs 20.2 actual), and the higher optimal time charge (7.84 vs the 5.66 billed) more than offsets the extra distance charge; you were not overcharged. A refund below SGD 0.50 is NO_ACTION as de minimis, and under POL-GEN-03 the charge stands as it is. 3. The Paya Lebar Quarter stop. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00112, weight 1.0) shows the request and the driver's 'ok can', but the trace never comes within 200 m of the resolved waypoint - the nearest fix is 512 m away (fix 158, 18:45:00). Under POL-RD-04 the corroboration test fails and POL-RD-14 directs that no distance is excluded; the instruction did not cause the measured excess. The missed stop is a service matter on which this policy pays nothing - no fare line charges a stop or a missed stop. The driver is also wrong to say he made the stop: his own device trace does not support it. 4. Impairment. EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are each impaired at weight 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT (they disagree about when the trip began by 13.5 minutes). That is schema-level impairment only: under POL-RD-07 the trace is policy-clean - no gap over 90 s (longest 0 s), no straight-line jump over 500 m, a 10 s sampling interval - so it still measures the excess, and the impairment enters POL-GEN-02 as a confidence discount, not as an escalation. 5. No escalation. POL-RD-10(1): the fact that decides this ruling - that the fare recomputation yields no refund - is carried by EV-FARE-00112 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0, line items reconciling to the cent); the 0.4 impairment goes to the measured actual distance, and the outcome is NO_ACTION whether or not a deviation is established. POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged, the trace being policy-clean. POL-RD-10(4) is not engaged: the pickup and dropoff events on the two records align (18:17:50 / 18:18:40 and 18:52:20 / 18:52:12); the divergence is the meter start, not a pickup or dropoff timestamp. POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged: the driver's 'the app was acting up' excuse cites no advisory, and POL-RD-13 makes an uncited traffic assertion weightless rather than an escalation. POL-RD-10(7) is confined by POL-RD-14: a request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent, not contradictory evidence. The rider's arguments for escalation on the 0.4 cap and on the started_at conflict are therefore rejected. 6. Other claims. No repeat-deviation pattern arises (1 flag over 296 trips in 90 days; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field POL-RD-06 names), so there is no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral. There are no ERP gantries, tolls, airport surcharge or promo lines, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct. The driver's compensation claim (2.4 unbilled km x 0.75 = 1.80) is declined: it rests entirely on the 0.4-weighted trace and on exactly the disputed pre-start segment, so it cannot be granted above the confidence floor. The monetary effect is nil, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00. Either party may appeal this provisional ruling under POL-GEN-04.
Trip TRP-00112 (Tampines to One Raffles Place, 4 Aug 2026; charged S$25.26). The charge stands and no refund is due to the rider; no compensation is due to the driver. 1) The fare. This was a METERED trip, so POL-RD-02 recomputes what the booked optimal route should have cost: base 3.80 + distance (0.75 x 17.6 km = 13.20) + time (0.28 x 28.0 min = 7.84) = 24.84, times the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown (and nowhere else), plus the 0.80 platform fee. No ERP, toll, airport surcharge, waiting fee or promo applies, so the recomputed fare is 25.64. The rider paid 25.26. The optimal-route fare is therefore HIGHER than what was charged, so the refund is negative, floors at zero, and is below the 0.50 de minimis: NO_ACTION, and the 25.26 stands (POL-RD-02, POL-GEN-03). The reason is the optimal route's 28.0-minute duration - the rider was billed for only 20.2 minutes, and that saving more than offsets the extra distance. 2) The distance conflict. The GPS trace begins at 18:18:40 and covers 2.38 km before the trip record's meter start of 18:32:10 - a 13 min 30 s disagreement. Both EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and that discount is carried through below. Measured over the whole trace the excess is 4.80 km / 27.27% (above the POL-RD-01 gate); measured over the recorded trip window it is 2.42 km / 13.8% (below it). I accept that nothing in the bundle conclusively decides which reading is right. It does not change the outcome: on the higher reading the deviation is established and POL-RD-02 still returns nothing (point 1); on the lower reading no deviation is established and POL-RD-01 gives the same NO_ACTION. The trace is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (no gaps, longest gap 0 s, 10 s sampling against the 30 s limb, no >500 m jumps), so the POL-RD-07 consequences and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation do not engage - the 0.4 is a POL-GEN-02 confidence down-weight only. 3) The Paya Lebar Quarter stop. I accept the rider asked for the stop (MSG-00112-001, carrying a resolved waypoint_hint at Paya Lebar Quarter) and the driver agreed ('ok can', MSG-00112-002). But an extra-stop instruction excludes distance only if the trace corroborates it, and the trace never comes within 200 m of the waypoint - the nearest fix is 512.35 m (fix 158, 18:45:00). Under POL-RD-14 the request therefore excluded no distance; the driver's statement that he made the stop is unsupported by his own trace and carries no weight (POL-RD-08). No fare line charges a stop or missed-stop fee, so the missed stop is a service matter on which this policy pays nothing. 4) The driver's 'app was acting up' explanation. Any external-traffic excuse is tested against this trip's traffic_advisory and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 - no LTA advisory covers the PIE/ECP window. Under POL-RD-13 the excuse is tested against nothing and carries no weight (POL-RD-08); POL-RD-03 is unavailable and reduces no excess. 5) Driver compensation. The driver's request for compensation for 'unbilled' distance is refused. It rests on the 2.4 km difference between the trace's 22.40 km and the billed 20.00 km, and that difference is exactly the contested pre-start head: the billed 20.00 km matches the trace after 18:32:10 (about 20.02 km). The same unresolved conflict that makes the deviation reading uncertain means the record does not establish that this distance was driven on this trip rather than carried over from a previous job, so no shortfall is established and nothing is paid. 6) Escalation and referrals. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The artifacts' pickup and dropoff events agree (arrival 18:17:50 vs first fix 18:18:40, 50 s; end 18:52:20 vs last fix 18:52:12, 8 s), so POL-RD-10(4) is not engaged - the divergence is the internal meter start, handled under POL-GEN-02 and immaterial either way. POL-RD-10(7) is confined by POL-RD-14 to the partly-corroborated case. POL-RD-10(1) is not engaged because the fact that decides the money sits on the clean EV-FARE-00112 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0), not on the impaired instruments. No billing-integrity defect exists under POL-RD-09(4). On POL-RD-06 the driver's trailing-90-day record (1 deviation flag over 296 completed trips) is below both limbs, so there is no pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral; no other profile field has been used (POL-GEN-01). Confidence 0.9: the deciding money facts (charged 25.26 and the recomputed 25.64) are carried by the clean fare_breakdown, so the ruling is not driven below the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect is nil, below the 8.00 execution threshold. Two claims were discarded at the citation check: a rider claim citing the missing traffic advisory without naming its issue code, and a driver claim citing the impaired trace without naming its issue code. This ruling was made without human review. Either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04.
To both parties. [Rider] — what you paid ($25.26) is less than what the booked optimal route would cost under the fare model, so there is nothing to refund, and the fare stands. The arithmetic (POL-RD-02): the booked optimal route (PIE westbound then ECP) is 17.6 km and 28.0 min. Recomputation = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 = 13.20 distance + 0.28 x 28.0 = 7.84 time) x surge 1.0 (read from the fare breakdown's surge_multiplier, and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee = $25.64. No ERP, tolls, surcharge, waiting fee or promo apply. $25.64 exceeds the $25.26 charged, so the refund floors at zero, and it is below the $0.50 de-minimis floor: NO_ACTION. Your route was longer (20.0 km vs 17.6 km) but your time was shorter (20.2 min vs 28.0 min), and the time saving ($2.18) more than offsets the extra distance ($1.80) — you were undercharged by about $0.38, not overcharged. Your deviation claim: the trace records 22.40 km against the 17.60 km optimal, a 4.80 km / 27.27% excess, which would clear the POL-RD-01 gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km), and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern the trip record's rounded 20.0 km. But the trace and the trip record disagree about when the trip began (18:18:40 vs 18:32:10 — 13 min 30 s), and measured from the recorded trip start the excess is only 2.42 km / 13.8%. The disagreement does not decide the money: on either figure the POL-RD-02 refund is nil. The Paya Lebar Quarter stop (POL-RD-04 / POL-RD-14): you asked for it (MSG-00112-001) and [driver] agreed ('ok can', MSG-00112-002), but the trace never comes within 200 m of the waypoint — the nearest fix is 512 m at 18:45:00 — so the instruction did not cause the excess, no distance is excluded, and the policy pays nothing for a missed stop: no stop fee appears on the receipt, and the distance-and-time lines recompute to zero. [Driver] — your account that you made the stop ('waited about four minutes there') is not supported: the trace never comes within 512 m of the waypoint, so it carries no weight (POL-RD-08). Your compensation claim for distance billed below the trace is refused: the 2.4 km shortfall is exactly the disputed pre-start segment, and against the recorded trip window the billed 20.0 km matches the 20.02 km driven, so no shortfall over 1.0 km is established. Evidence and confidence: EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are both IMPAIRED on the pre-pass at weight 0.4, issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT — an alignment defect between the trace and the trip record. It is not a POL-RD-07 defect: the trace has no gap over 90 s (max 0 s), no jump over 500 m, and a 10 s sampling interval, so it is policy-clean and governs the POL-RD-01 threshold. The impairment is disclosed and priced into confidence, but the deciding arithmetic (the zero refund) is carried by the COMPLETE fare breakdown at weight 1.0, so it does not cap the ruling below the 0.70 floor. Confidence 0.80. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral: 1 deviation flag over 296 trips is neither the 3-flag nor the 0.05-ratio test, and the deviation is not MATERIAL (4.80 km < 8.0 km; 27.3% < 50%). No POL-RD-09(4) billing finding: there is no ERP, toll or surcharge line, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. No POL-RD-10 escalation: the trip identifiers match, the pickup and dropoff events align across the artifacts (arrival 18:17:50 vs first fix 18:18:40; ended_at 18:52:20 vs last fix 18:52:12), the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), and the uncorroborated PLQ instruction is a failed corroboration (POL-RD-14), not the contradiction POL-RD-10(7) describes. The monetary effect is nil, below the $8.00 execution threshold. The contested amount was $6.00; none of it is refunded.
